project.name: curl
project.commit_note: The staged vulnerable source under `_work/src/curl` is used for exact line mapping and matches the saved ASan frames at `seturl:856/887/930`, `curl_url_set:1359`, and `Curl_follow:1593`. Upstream fix commit `02c6b984cb7a2e01f290544a53a24d30fc7ab32e` adds `u->temppath` and an HTTP regression test, but the staged witness reproduced here reaches the same lifetime bug through HTTP auth retry rather than a `Location:` header.

classification.classification_note: The saved crash is a free-before-use of a temporary encoded path buffer inside `seturl()`: `query` aliases bytes inside that buffer, `Curl_dedotdotify()` returns a different normalized path for the witness's `/./` segment, and the changed-path branch at `seturl()` lines 884-887 frees the temporary `path` buffer before `u->query = strdup(query)` copies the aliased query bytes. The staged witness reaches this path during HTTP authentication retry, not through `Location:` redirect handling.

bug_description.original: OSS-Fuzz issue 42478820 (curl): Heap-use-after-free READ 6 found by fuzz target curl_fuzzer_http [asan]. https://issues.oss-fuzz.com/issues/42478820
bug_description.original_source: sample_info.json issue_description / staged sanitizer_trace.txt / staged poc / patch.diff / reproduction_report.json
bug_description.normalized: The staged `poc` is a 157-byte TLV stream with exactly three records: TLV 1 (`URL`, length 37) carries the raw scheme-less URL bytes `20` x18, `40 ff ff ff 2f 2e 2f 20` x8, `3f 20 20 20`; TLV 2 (`RESPONSE0`, length 98) supplies an `HTTP/2 401` response whose header block begins `WWW-Authenticate: DIgest`; and TLV 16 (`HTTPAUTH`, length 4) sets `CURLOPT_HTTPAUTH` to `0x202020ff`. In libcurl, `parseurlandfillconn()` first parses the URL TLV with `CURLU_GUESS_SCHEME`, so the malformed string becomes the current URL object and its pre-`@` userinfo makes `conn->bits.user_passwd = TRUE`. When curl later parses the staged 401 challenge, `Curl_http_input_auth()` marks Digest available and `Curl_http_auth_act()` clones the original raw URL string into `data->req.newurl`. `multi_runsingle()` then routes that clone through `Curl_follow()` as a FOLLOW_REDIR-style reparse, so `curl_url_set(..., CURLU_URLENCODE)` receives the same scheme-less string as `part`. Because `Curl_is_absolute_url(part)` is false on this path, `curl_url_set()` first builds `redired_url = concat_url(oldurl, part)` and then `seturl(redired_url, ...)` allocates a temporary encoded `path` buffer at line 856. `seturl()` next derives `query` as an interior pointer into that buffer, then calls `Curl_dedotdotify(path)`. The witness-derived `/./` segment makes `strcmp(newp, path)` true, so line 887 frees the temporary `path` buffer before `query` has been copied anywhere else. Line 930 immediately executes `u->query = strdup(query)`, and `curl_dbg_strdup`/`strlen` read from the freed heap region. The saved ASan report shows the allocation at `seturl:856`, the free at `seturl:887`, and the use at `seturl:930`. The fix resolves this exact lifetime obligation by tracking the temporary path buffer in `u->temppath` and deferring its free until after `u->path`, `u->query`, and `u->fragment` have been duplicated.

source.code:
uc = curl_url_set(uh, CURLUPART_URL, data->change.url,
                    CURLU_GUESS_SCHEME |
                    CURLU_NON_SUPPORT_SCHEME |
                    (data->set.disallow_username_in_url ?
                     CURLU_DISALLOW_USER : 0) |
                    (data->set.path_as_is ? CURLU_PATH_AS_IS : 0));
source.description: First project parser statement that consumes the attacker-controlled URL TLV and materializes the current libcurl URL handle used later as `oldurl` during the crashing auth retry reparse.
source.value_from: The staged URL TLV value is exactly 37 bytes: `20` x18, then `40 ff ff ff`, then `2f 2e 2f`, then `20` x8, then `3f 20 20 20`. In Latin-1 this is `"                  @\xff\xff\xff/./        ?   "`.

sink.description: First project-level use of the dangling query alias. `strdup(query)` enters `curl_dbg_strdup` and then ASan's intercepted `strlen`, which reports the heap-use-after-free read.
sink.note: The saved ASan stack is `strlen -> curl_dbg_strdup -> seturl:930 -> parseurl -> curl_url_set:1359 -> Curl_follow:1593`, so this statement is the exact project sink that feeds the runtime crash.

root_cause.description: Root cause. When `Curl_dedotdotify(path)` returns a changed path, the vulnerable branch frees the temporary encoded `path` buffer even though `query` still aliases bytes inside that buffer and has not yet been duplicated.
root_cause.note: The fix adds `u->temppath` precisely to hold whichever temporary buffer `path` currently aliases and frees it only after `u->path`, `u->query`, and `u->fragment` are copied.

coarse_trace.summary: The staged TLV stream installs one malformed scheme-less URL, one `HTTP/2 401` response containing `WWW-Authenticate: DIgest`, and an `HTTPAUTH` bitmask that allows Digest.

libcurl parses that raw URL with `CURLU_GUESS_SCHEME`, preserves its `/./...?...` tail in the URL handle, and marks the connection as carrying user credentials because the string has userinfo before `@`.
`Curl_pretransfer()` copies the staged `CURLOPT_HTTPAUTH` bitmask into `data->state.authhost.want`, preparing the later `pickoneauth()` decision.
While parsing the staged `HTTP/2 401` response, `Curl_http_readwrite_headers()` recognizes the `WWW-Authenticate:` header, copies its value into `auth`, and forwards it to `Curl_http_input_auth()`.
`checkprefix("Digest", auth)` matches the copied `DIgest...` challenge, so curl marks Digest available and stores the challenge parameters.
`pickoneauth()` intersects the available methods with the wanted bitmask and, on success, clones the original raw URL into `data->req.newurl` for auth retry.
Because `data->req.newurl` is set, `multi_runsingle()` moves it into local `newurl`, clears `data->req.newurl`, and tags the handoff as `FOLLOW_REDIR`.
`Curl_follow()` reparses that same scheme-less retry URL with `curl_url_set(..., CURLU_URLENCODE)`.
Because the retry URL is still relative, `curl_url_set()` builds `redired_url = concat_url(oldurl, part)` and reparses the concatenated URL.

`seturl()` allocates a temporary encoded path buffer, derives `query` as an interior alias into it, frees that buffer when `Curl_dedotdotify()` changes the `/./` path, and then `u->query = strdup(query)` reads through the dangling alias.

fine_trace.note: Harness step. The staged TLV stream has exactly three records: URL TLV 1 sets `CURLOPT_URL` to raw bytes `20` x18 `40 ff ff ff 2f 2e 2f 20` x8 `3f 20 20 20`; RESPONSE0 TLV 2 sets the first server reply to `HTTP/2 401` with a `WWW-Authenticate: DIgest...` header; and HTTPAUTH TLV 16 sets `CURLOPT_HTTPAUTH = 0x202020ff`, whose low bits include `CURLAUTH_DIGEST`.

fine_trace.code:
uc = curl_url_set(uh, CURLUPART_URL, data->change.url,
                    CURLU_GUESS_SCHEME |
                    CURLU_NON_SUPPORT_SCHEME |
                    (data->set.disallow_username_in_url ?
                     CURLU_DISALLOW_USER : 0) |
                    (data->set.path_as_is ? CURLU_PATH_AS_IS : 0));
fine_trace.note: Source. libcurl first parses the URL TLV here. Because the string has no scheme, `CURLU_GUESS_SCHEME` makes this parse treat it as an HTTP URL and store the result in `data->state.uh`, preserving the witness's `/./` path segment and `?   ` query tail for later retries.

The 18 leading space bytes before `@` are parsed as the URL's user component. `curl_url_get(..., CURLUPART_USER, ...)` therefore succeeds and sets `conn->bits.user_passwd = TRUE`, which is a prerequisite for the later 401 host-auth retry branch.

Before the transfer starts, curl copies the `CURLOPT_HTTPAUTH` value previously set from TLV 16 into `data->state.authhost.want`. This is the `pick->want` bitmask that `pickoneauth()` later intersects with the methods advertised by the 401 challenge.

When curl reads RESPONSE0 from step 0, `Curl_http_readwrite_headers()` takes this 401-auth branch, sets `proxy = FALSE`, copies the `WWW-Authenticate` value into heap string `auth`, and hands that string to `Curl_http_input_auth()`.

`checkprefix` is case-insensitive, so the copied `DIgest...` challenge from step 4 matches `Digest`. This records Digest as an available host-auth method and stores its parameters for later use. The later retry proves `Curl_input_digest()` did not reject this challenge.

In the 401 host-auth branch, `pickoneauth()` computes `pick->avail & pick->want & authmask`. With Digest available from step 5 and allowed by step 3's bitmask, it returns TRUE and selects host auth instead of `CURLAUTH_PICKNONE`.

Inside the `if(pickhost || pickproxy)` branch, curl clones the original raw URL string from step 0 into `data->req.newurl`. This is the auth-retry URL; no `Location:` header is involved on the reproduced path.

Because step 7 made `data->req.newurl` non-NULL and this path is not a connection retry, `multi_runsingle()` takes the `!retry` arm, moves the cloned auth-retry URL into local `newurl`, clears `data->req.newurl`, and tags the handoff as `FOLLOW_REDIR`. The saved stack's `multi_runsingle:2042 -> Curl_follow:1593` frames place this dispatcher immediately before the crashing reparse.

Step 8 passes the cloned scheme-less URL into `Curl_follow()` with `type == FOLLOW_REDIR`, so this call reparses the auth-retry URL with `CURLU_URLENCODE` even though no `Location:` header is involved.

The retry string forwarded in steps 8-9 is still scheme-less, so `Curl_is_absolute_url(part, NULL, MAX_SCHEME_LEN + 1)` is false and the saved ASan frame `curl_url_set:1359` comes from this relative-URL branch. curl retrieves the current canonical URL from step 1 as `oldurl`, concatenates it with the retry `part`, and passes the resulting `redired_url` into `parseurl()`. That concatenated URL still carries the witness-derived `/./` path segment and query tail.

Inside the nested `seturl(redired_url, ...)` parse, the flags from step 9 still contain `CURLU_URLENCODE` and the parsed path is non-empty, so curl allocates a new heap buffer, copies the path into it with URL-encoding rules, marks `path_alloced = TRUE`, and rebinds `path` to this buffer. ASan reports this exact line-856 allocation site.

After step 11 has placed the parsed path in a temporary heap buffer, this code finds the query separator derived from the witness's `?   ` suffix. `*query++ = 0` terminates the path in-place and leaves `query` as an interior alias into the same line-856 buffer.

Root cause. The witness-derived `/./` segment makes `Curl_dedotdotify(path)` return a different string, so `strcmp(newp, path)` is true. Because step 11 already set `path_alloced = TRUE`, line 887 frees the only buffer backing step 12's `query` alias before `query` has been duplicated or rebased. The fix introduces `u->temppath` specifically to defer this free until after the later copies complete.

Sink. `query` still points into the freed line-856 buffer from step 13, so `strdup(query)` reaches `curl_dbg_strdup` and then the intercepted `strlen` on freed memory. ASan reports `heap-use-after-free` with `READ of size 4` at runtime frame 0 and this line as the first project frame.

allocation_context.description: ASan allocation site for the temporary encoded `path` buffer that later backs `query`.

free_context.description: ASan free site for the same temporary encoded `path` buffer before `query` is duplicated.

sanitizer_ground_truth.patch_resolves_note: Yes at the source level. The fix adds `u->temppath`, stores whichever temporary buffer `path` currently aliases, and frees that storage only after `u->path`, `u->query`, and `u->fragment` have been duplicated. That removes the free-before-`strdup(query)` condition shown in fine-trace steps 11-14.

format.name: curl_fuzzer_http TLV stream
format.contract: Exactly the staged 157-byte TLV stream stored at `poc`. It contains only three records: TLV 1 (`URL`, length 37) with bytes `20` x18 `40 ff ff ff 2f 2e 2f 20` x8 `3f 20 20 20`; TLV 2 (`RESPONSE0`, length 98) whose payload begins `HTTP/2 401  \nWWW-Authenticate: DIgest`; and TLV 16 (`HTTPAUTH`, length 4) with value `0x202020ff`. That exact combination makes libcurl parse the scheme-less URL once, set `conn->bits.user_passwd` from the pre-`@` userinfo, accept the 401 host-auth challenge, clone the same raw URL into `data->req.newurl`, and re-enter `curl_url_set` through FOLLOW_REDIR-style auth retry. On the witnessed path, the retry parse must still contain the witness's `/./` path segment and `?   ` query suffix so that `seturl()` allocates a temporary encoded path buffer, derives `query` as an interior alias into it, frees that buffer when `Curl_dedotdotify()` changes the path, and then reaches `u->query = strdup(query)`. The staged artifacts do not justify a broader trigger beyond this exact TLV layout and observed auth-retry reparse path.
